correctness.rationale: A4 on four points is 2-transitive: the stabilizer of any point is cyclic of order three on the other points, hence primitive. For f=(0,0,1,1), X={0,1}, Y={2,3}, ordered image pairs under either any even permutation or f stay among (singleton,singleton), (same 2-subset,same 2-subset), and (complementary 2-subsets). Thus every transformation in M=<A4,f> maps X,Y to sets of equal size; no map collapses precisely one to a singleton, violating Hoffmann strong sync-maximality. Independently generated A4 (12 permutations) and full transformation monoid (52 elements), verified the equality for every element. The invariant proof establishes the complete nonexistence claim.

originality.rationale: Hoffmann 2021 defines strong sync-maximality and proves 4-transitive implies strong implies primitive, explicitly posing whether containments are proper. A4 is a well-known primitive non-4-transitive group, but that alone does not refute strong sync-maximality; the explicit rank-2 map and invariant supply the missing counterexample to the upper inclusion. The later primitive automata paper addresses a different synchronization condition. No earlier exact A4 strong-property witness was located in targeted searches.
residual_risks: An unindexed post-Hoffmann note could contain the same degree-four example.
The separation proves only the upper containment strict; no statement about proper inclusion of 4-transitive groups is implied.

value.rationale: The small degree-four counterexample resolves the mathematically explicit strictness question for strongly sync-maximal versus primitive groups. The invariant gives a reusable obstruction by complementary-pair symmetry, beyond a naked computational table. It does not settle the lower 4-transitive inclusion or higher-degree classification.
